subproblem.title: Dilations of currents in ℝ^P exist and agree with the blow-up η_{a,λ#}
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − a). For X, X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ m) say that X' is a dilation of X if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Then (i) every X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) has a dilation X'; and (ii) if X' is a dilation of X, then X'(ω) = η_{a,λ#}X(ω₁) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and every ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P)) (TestFormOn (dilation a λ '' univ) m) whose underlying differential form equals that of ω, where η_{a,λ#}X = blowUp X a λ ∈ 𝒟_m(η(ℝ^P)) is the contract's blow-up (proper affine push-forward of X by η).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, ∃ X' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ ω ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (dilation a lam y)) → X' ω = lam⁻¹ ^ m * X ω')) ∧ ∀ X X' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ ω ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (dilation a lam y)) → X' ω = lam⁻¹ ^ m * X ω') → ∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (ω₁ : TestFormOn (dilation a lam '' (univ : Set (Euclid P))) m), (ω₁ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) → X' ω = blowUp X a lam hlam.ne' ω₁
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof (the dilation is the affine push-forward of X by η; X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω∘η)), specialized through the sibling testform_correspondence, which is the same computation for blowUp in an arbitrary domain U; here U = ℝ^P.
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P; η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − a), λ > 0. For V ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(V) = TestFormOn V k is the space of C^∞ k-forms ω on ℝ^P (maps to k-covectors) with compact tsupport ω ⊆ V; its elements are determined by their underlying forms. 𝒟_k(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V k. For X, X' ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), X' is a dilation of X when X'(ω) = λ^{−k}X(ω') for all ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. η_#Y := η_{a,λ#}Y = blowUp Y a λ ∈ 𝒟_k(η(U)) for Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U). Sibling names refer to the children of this decomposition: testform_correspondence = dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr, blowup_structure = dtc_blowUp_algebra, rep_pushforward = dtc_blowUp_imrep, mass_scaling = dtc_blowUp_massOn_image, dilation_blowup = cbr_cidc_dilation_exists_eq_blowUp.
1. Surjectivity. η is onto ℝ^P: for y ∈ ℝ^P, η(a + λy) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹(a + λy) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹a + (λ⁻¹λ)y = y because λ ≠ 0. Hence ℝ^P ⊆ η(ℝ^P), i.e. η(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, so every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) is also an element of 𝒟^k(η(ℝ^P)) with the same underlying form (tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P ⊆ η(ℝ^P); SimonGMT testFormOnInclusion), and every element of 𝒟^k(η(ℝ^P)) is an element of 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with the same underlying form. Moreover every current Y ∈ 𝒟_m(η(ℝ^P)) restricts to a current Y|ℝ^P ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P), Y|ℝ^P(ω) := Y(ω regarded in 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P))) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain along ℝ^P ⊆ η(ℝ^P): the composite of Y with the linear inclusion is linear, and it is sequentially continuous because a sequence converging in 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with supports in a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P also converges in 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P)) with the same K ⊆ η(ℝ^P)).
2. Proof of (i). Let X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and put X'' := (η_#X)|ℝ^P ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P), so X''(ω) = η_#X(ω̂) where ω̂ ∈ 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P)) is ω regarded in η(ℝ^P). Let ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y. As ω̂ and ω have the same underlying form, ω'(y) = ω̂(η(y)) for all y. testform_correspondence (c), applied with U = ℝ^P, x = a, n = m, T = X and the pair ω̂ ∈ 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P)), ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), gives η_#X(ω̂) = λ^{−m}X(ω'). Hence X''(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω'), i.e. X'' is a dilation of X.
3. Proof of (ii). Let X' be a dilation of X, let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), and let ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P)) have the same underlying form as ω. By testform_correspondence (a) (U = ℝ^P, x = a, n = m) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω₁(η(y)) for all y; since ω₁ and ω have the same underlying form, also ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y.
4. By testform_correspondence (c) (U = ℝ^P, x = a, T = X, the pair ω₁, ω'), η_#X(ω₁) = λ^{−m}X(ω'). By the dilation property of X' applied to the pair ω, ω', X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω'). Therefore X'(ω) = η_#X(ω₁), proving (ii). No hypothesis on m was used (m = 0 included). ∎
Formalization notes (proved in a scratch build from the exact sibling type): hsurj : univ ⊆ dilation a λ '' univ via ⟨a + λ • y, mem_univ _, by simp [dilation, dilationCLM, smul_add, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hlam.ne']⟩; for (i) take (blowUp X a λ hlam.ne').restrictDomain hsurj and rewrite with GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply, then apply part (c) of the sibling (the hypothesis transfers by simpa, testFormOnInclusion_coe being rfl); for (ii) obtain ω' from part (a) and rewrite with part (c) and the dilation hypothesis.
proof_key_steps: η(a + λy) = y, so η(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P: test forms in ℝ^P and in η(ℝ^P) are the same forms, and η_#X restricts to a current on ℝ^P.
(i) The restriction of η_#X to ℝ^P is a dilation of X by testform_correspondence (c).
(ii) For a dilation X' and equal underlying forms ω, ω₁, both X'(ω) and η_#X(ω₁) equal λ^{−m}X(ω∘η), where ω∘η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) exists by testform_correspondence (a).

audit.reason: Surjectivity justifies restricting the blow-up to univ. Test-form correspondence proves both existence and equality of evaluations for every pair with equal underlying forms, exactly matching the two conclusions.
